statement: When Ann was as old as Bo is now, Bo was 6. When Bo is as old as Ann is now, Ann will be 30. How old is Ann now?

choices.misconception: I found Bo's age now instead of Ann's.
I assumed Ann's age now is exactly halfway between 6 and 30.
I found the age gap between Ann and Bo and gave that as Ann's age.
I gave Ann's age at the later moment, not her age now.

hints: The gap between their ages is always the same.
Draw a line of ages with four marks: Bo's age back then, Bo's age now, Ann's age now and Ann's age later. Each pair of neighbouring marks is exactly one age gap apart.
The ages 6, Bo's age now, Ann's age now and 30 are equally spaced, so there are three equal gaps from 6 to 30.

solutions.reliable: Let the age gap be $g$. Ann was Bo's current age $g$ years ago, when Bo was 6, so Bo is now $6 + g$ and Ann is $6 + 2g$. Bo reaches Ann's current age in $g$ years, when Ann will be $6 + 3g = 30$. So $g = 8$, Bo is 14 and Ann is 22. Check: 8 years ago Ann was 14 and Bo was 6; in 8 years Bo will be 22 and Ann 30. The transferable idea: in 'when A was as old as B is now' problems, each shift in time is exactly one age gap.

whyOnTest: Tangled age statements become simple once you see that every shift in time is one age gap; the test is turning the words into equally spaced ages.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
